3) Do snapshots/backups ever cross international borders for the purpose of disaster recovery?
4) Are any ephemeral caches or model KV caches considered customer data and retained after request completion?

Hi Anna — thanks for the focused list. Below are concise answers you can paste into your RFP spreadsheet; I included the operational detail beneath each response for your internal reviewers.

Short answers (for questionnaire):
• Primary storage: customer content for Hosted API tenants is stored in the customer-selected region (primary AZs within that region).
• Backups: periodic backups and short-term snapshots are stored in the same geographic region by default; asynchronously replicated to a paired failover region within the same country/geo only when cross-AZ failover is configured. We do not replicate hosted-tenant content to a region in a different legal jurisdiction for routine DR.
• Deletion timeline: deletion requests are acknowledged immediately; primary-store deletion is completed within 72 hours. Backup/snapshot eviction follows the backup retention window (see below) and is scheduled to remove copies outside normal recovery windows (typically within 30 days).
• Ephemeral/model caches: runtime KV and prompt caches are ephemeral and not persisted to long-term storage; they are flushed on request completion and not included in backups.

Operational detail (paste where you need more context):
1) Data residency: when provisioning a tenant on our Hosted API you choose a primary region (e.g., us-west-2). Customer content (requests, generated outputs, metadata tied to tenant IDs) is written to primary persistent storage within that region (multi-AZ for availability). For customers that enable cross-region DR, we replicate metadata-only failover pointers to the configured secondary region; full-data cross-region replication is only done with explicit contractual approval and documented in the DPA/contract.

2) Backups & snapshots: our platform takes encrypted incremental snapshots of tenant data for operational recovery. By default snapshots are stored in the same region; snapshots are retained according to the retention tier: standard (30 days) for the bulk of Hosted API customers. Longer snapshot horizons (90/365 days) are available as an add-on. Snapshots are encrypted with customer-tenant keys (KMS) for enterprise customers where requested. We do not routinely copy snapshots to another country. For disaster recovery we support failover configurations that keep data within the same legal geo (US / EU / APAC) unless a customer explicitly requests otherwise.

3) Deletion flow: a deletion request can be initiated via the Console or the Admin API. The flow is: (a) mark tenant objects for deletion and remove from primary indexes (fast path); (b) background job expunges objects from primary stores (up to 72 hours); (c) snapshot lifecycle controller queues associated snapshot segments for eviction. Snapshots are immutable while retained — eviction completes per the retention policy window (default 30 days). We provide an erasure receipt for primary-store completion and a separate confirmation when all recoverable snapshots are evicted (if requested).

4) Caches & model artifacts: transient runtime caches (prompt prefixes, KV caches) are stored in-memory or ephemeral local SSD on the serving nodes and are zeroed on process shutdown; they are not written to long-term persistent stores and are not included in backups. Model weights or transformer artifacts are never mixed with tenant-specific content.

Evidence & docs: Attached is our current retention matrix (redwood_retention_matrix_v2.xlsx) and a simplified erase-flow diagram. For SOC 2 / audit evidence we can provide a sanitized runbook and the attestation excerpt showing deletion receipts.

If you want, we can: (1) produce a one-page statement for your procurement pack, (2) provide DPA language for an EU/US-only geography guarantee, or (3) schedule a 30-min call to walk through logs/receipts. Which would you prefer?

Hi Anna — quick follow-up to address A/B.

A) Snapshot irrecoverability: our default operational model treats snapshots as immutable objects for the duration of their retention window to preserve RPO guarantees. For deleted tenant content we offer two mechanisms to reduce the recoverability window:
  1) Targeted snapshot eviction: when a tenant requests immediate purge we can prioritize any live snapshots that contain the tenant's segments for eviction (this shortens the practical exposure but does not change the underlying immutability model of standard snapshots). Eviction typically completes within the configured snapshot purge cadence and we can accelerate to force removal within 7–14 days for an approved operational runbook.
  2) Key scoping & rotation: for enterprise customers we support tenant-scoped envelope encryption where snapshots are encrypted with a tenant-specific data key. Upon deletion we can destroy the tenant data key (cryptographic shredding), which renders older snapshots unreadable almost immediately even if the blobs remain in object storage. This requires an agreed contract addendum and is available for customers requiring strong irrecoverability guarantees.

B) Erasure receipt contents & sample: the erasure receipt is a signed statement containing: tenant id, deletion request id, timestamp of primary-store purge completion, list of object namespaces/IDs that were purged from primary indexes, a reference ID for the snapshot eviction job, and the operator run-id that initiated the purge. For enterprise customers we can provide a signed JSON receipt and an audit log extract showing the background job progression. I attached a sanitized example receipt and the erase_flow_diagram.png to this thread for your pack.

Next steps — deliverables we can get to you this week if that works:

• Redlineable DPA stub with a geo-lock clause and tenant-scoped key options.
• Sanitized sample erasure receipt (JSON) and the retention matrix we already attached.
